themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models start by building a small set of cases they can actually prove, then grade everything else against that.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization all three models build a fixed panel of real buyer questions because answers are non-deterministic; on identity resolution Claude freezes a list of multi-device logins as a truth set and ChatGPT calls representative ground truth the core blocker; on incrementality the platform re-optimizes against the holdout; on agentic traffic the models label sessions from confirmed agent orders.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a dollar, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from the outside and hoping the behavior matches the promise.
themes.evidence: On provable downstream consent and deletion, Claude says proof in agency and partner copies rests on contracts and canaries rather than architecture, ChatGPT traces a seeded opt-out through a single ad audience, and Gemini calls trained model weights a place an individual cannot be unlearned; the same opacity shows up in agent execution, identity resolution and ad supply integrity.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Today on downstream consent, Claude puts every exit behind one logged checkpoint and Gemini cuts syncs to systems without deletion APIs; agent execution answers repeatedly propose a proxy or gateway with hard spend and audience caps, and journey orchestration answers propose a shared send log or kill switch that every channel must check.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning and worth, not data: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, what the word customer means, how wrong a match is allowed to be. No formula settles these, because the disagreement usually has budget attached.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three models say implied meaning and tone decide liability and cannot be checked by software; on the semantic context layer they call conflicting definitions of active customer a political settlement rather than a modeling gap; on journey orchestration they say no agreed number prices a sale today against fatigue tomorrow.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by handing it over, and nobody can force them. So the models either try to make honesty pay better than hiding, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work only with what they already own.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic the models build a fast declared-agent lane with better prices because agents gain by looking human; on incrementality platforms control both the treatment and the evidence; on journey orchestration channel owners subvert coordination that cuts their credited numbers; on ad supply integrity the parties measuring the traffic profit from it.
